answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce a quadratic deposit mechanism where each new identity must lock increasing collateral into a secure vault. Registering n replicas requires locking stake that scales superlinearly as O(n^2), while malicious deviations trigger cryptographic stake burning that converts the vault funds into unrecoverable basalt dust. For transient flash-loan attackers, validation windows flash past like a fleeting comet, imposing exponential capital costs that render multi-identity flooding economically impossible.
